title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-zoe-li
content:
PR: optimize-kv-cache-batching (runtime/pull/2345) - scratchpad
Owner: Zoe Li
Context: This PR touches KV cache eviction, batch formation, and a small refactor to the request coalescer. Goal is to reduce tail latency for short requests and improve GPU utilization for mixed workloads.

High-level notes:
- Concern: changing eviction timing + batcher window could interact badly under high qps; need load test matrix.
- The new eviction heuristic (freq-based decay) seems promising but complexity spike around remaining_ttl calc. Could simplify to moving average count instead.
- Coalescer refactor removes the per-request mutex but adds atomic counters — check false-sharing and cache-line alignment implications.

Review checklist (initial pass):
- [ ] Correctness: ensure no new race conditions in coalescer + cache update path. Look for places where we read-modify-write without proper barriers.
- [ ] Tests: unit tests updated? There are a couple of small tests in cache_test.go but no end-to-end for batching under load. Add integration test that simulates 1000 qps with mixed seq lengths.
- [ ] Benchmarks: add microbench for eviction path and for coalescer under contention (10/50/100 concurrent). Capture allocations.
- [ ] Telemetry: new metrics introduced (kv.evictions.*) - update dashboards & alert rules (pager config?).
- [ ] Config validation: ensure new config fields (eviction_decay_ms, batch_max_delay_ms) have sane boundaries and defaults; document in config reference.
- [ ] Backward compatibility: new evictions persisted format? Confirm on-disk snapshot compatibility (if any).
- [ ] Security: no user-provided values used to index arrays; double-check any parsing of header metadata.

Potential refactors / simplifications:
- Replace remaining_ttl computation with exponential moving average of hit intervals — easier to reason and likely as effective.
- Move atomic counters into a padded struct to avoid false sharing (pad to 64 bytes). Add a comment referencing redwood-infra-docs/perf-guidelines.
- Extract batch formation into a separate file with small state machine and unit tests (easier to test deterministic scenarios).

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- TODO: Add an integration test under infra/perf that runs the workload from the PR description (small tokLen=8 fast requests + occasional long ones) and record p95/p99 latency with old vs new logic. (Assigned to: Avery)
- TODO: Instrument cache hit path with a lightweight sampling profiler to capture hot CPU paths during high qps. (Assigned to: Zoe)
- TODO: Update runbook: if evictions spike > 500/min, fallback to legacy eviction by toggling feature flag. Add Grafana panel.
- TODO: Open a small RFC about eviction heuristics for cross-team review (link once opened).

Quick code pointers:
- coalescer.go: lines ~120-220: verify atomic sequence — suspect missing memory_order_release on success path.
- kv_cache/evict.go: look at edge case where ttl_ms == 0 -> becomes division by zero in compute_score. Need fix.
- batcher/strategy.go: ensure batch_max_delay_ms used consistently; current code has hard-coded 5ms in one branch.

Questions for author (leave as comment in PR):
- Why did we choose decay window = 10s? Any data to support that vs 5s/30s?
- Could we start with conservative defaults (longer ttl) and then be more aggressive in a canary?

Suggested reviewers:
- @avery-kim (batching/throughput), @ethan-roberts (eviction heuristics), @samir-shah (SRE, telemetry)

Local test plan (quick):
1) Run unit tests: make test ./...
2) Run microbench: go test -bench=Evict -benchmem ./kv_cache -run=^$
3) Start local docker-based load generator: tools/loadgen --qps 200 --mix short:90,long:10 --duration 2m
4) Observe p95/p99 on local grafana (dev stack)

Notes to self / messy thoughts:
- If we make batcher wait up to batch_max_delay_ms, we might improve throughput at the expense of added latency for short requests. Maybe make batch_max_delay adaptive based on recent queue length? Could be a follow-up feature.
- Might consider an optimization where long sequences bypass batching and acquire a dedicated worker to avoid head-of-line blocking. Need to simulate.
- The coalescer atomic change was probably safe, but there are subtle ordering issues when combined with the cache write-back path. Add comments and assertions in debug builds.

Slack refs:
- thread: #eng-serving-runtime "kv cache patch" (see messages around Feb 25)
- local TODO: ping @avery on Monday for perf tests scheduling

End of scratchpad.

(Will attach to PR as a review comment and keep iterating.)
